title: Cap. 1 subject: Scripture sense — means & praedamnatio presuppose sin
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless, because sacred Scripture, and the glory of the Fathers Augustine, seem through predestination and reprobation to understand not mere and sole election unto the end, nor mere passing by or non election unto such an end, but at the same time to conjoin with the decree of giving the end, the decree of preparing and giving certain, designated, and infallible means unto the end; and with the decree of permitting someone to fail from the end, to couple another decree, of punishing and eternally damning him who failed; for this cause, I say, I think better and more fitting, I add also truer in this sense, that foreseen sin be presupposed as a condition of the subject, into which the decree of such predestination and reprobation falls. As to Scripture, through predestination it is accustomed to denote not bare designation unto the end of glory, but destination unto glory through means; nor through any means whatsoever, but through means of efficacious grace derived from Christ our Head and Mediator. Those places make for this; Ephesians 1:4. He elected you in him that we might be holy. 2 Timothy 1:9. He saved us from his purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ before secular times. From which places, and many others which could be heaped up, it is clear that the Apostle through predestination understands destination and direction unto the end of glory through infallible means of efficacious grace to be derived from Christ. Concerning Augustine it is more known than that it needs many things, that he through predestination designates the preparation of grace infallibly leading through unto glory. Famous is that definition, Predestination is the preparation of the benefits of God, by which whoever are liberated are most certainly liberated. Whence Aquinas describes predestination to be an act of special providence ordering and directing the elect unto the end of salvation, not through any means whatsoever, but through such as will infallibly produce the event itself. Let this therefore be taken: that Predestination as it is used in the Scriptures designates not an abstract decree, concerning the end alone, but a decree as it were complicated, concerning giving the end of eternal life through means of grace in Christ. Now as to Reprobation, from the use of the Scriptures it designates not bare passing by or non election, but predamnation or deputation unto destruction, which coheres by an inseparable bond with non election or passing by, at least as to the event. This is plain from thence, that the reprobate are called in the Scriptures vessels of wrath fitted unto destruction, Romans 9:22. Formerly written unto damnation, Jude 4. And Augustine calls reprobation predestination unto destruction. Under the vocabulary of reprobation therefore we ought to comprehend not the bare decree of passing by, or of not electing some, but moreover the will of predamning them. These things having been posited, I say such predestination and reprobation cannot rightly be conceived or explained, unless sin having been preconceived, as a common condition in the subject itself.
pass_b_english: Yet Scripture and Augustine, glory of the Fathers, do not take predestination and reprobation as bare election to the end, or bare passing-by. With the decree to give the end they join the decree to prepare and give certain, designated, infallible means; with the decree to permit falling short of the end they couple another — to punish and damn forever the one who fell short. For that reason I judge it better, fitter, and in this sense truer that foresight of sin be presupposed as a condition of the subject on which such a decree of predestination and reprobation falls. In Scripture predestination usually means not bare designation to glory's end, but destination to glory through means — and not any means, but means of efficacious grace derived from Christ our Head and Mediator. So Ephesians 1:4: he chose us in him that we should be holy; 2 Timothy 1:9: he saved us according to his purpose and the grace given us in Christ before the ages. From these and many like them it is plain the Apostle means destination and direction to glory's end by infallible means of efficacious grace from Christ. Augustine, as everyone knows, takes predestination as preparation of the grace that leads infallibly to glory: Predestination is the preparation of God's benefits by which whoever are set free are set free with certainty. So Aquinas describes it as special providence ordering and directing the elect to salvation's end not by any means, but by means that produce the event infallibly. Take it thus: Predestination in Scripture is not an abstract decree about the end alone, but a compounded decree — to give eternal life through means of grace in Christ. Reprobation in Scripture's use is not bare passing-by or non-election, but pre-damnation — appointment to destruction — bound inseparably to non-election, at least as to the event. Scripture calls the reprobate vessels of wrath fitted for destruction ([[Romans 9:22 >> Bible:Romans 9:22]]); formerly marked out for condemnation ([[Jude 4 >> Bible:Jude 4]]). Augustine calls reprobation predestination to destruction. Under "reprobation" we must include not only the bare decree to pass by, but also the will to pre-damn. That kind of predestination and reprobation cannot be conceived or explained rightly unless sin is preconceived as a common condition in the subject.
source_text: Veruntamen, quia sacra Scriptura, & decus Patrum Augustinus, videntur per praedestinationem & reprobationem, non meram & solam electionem ad finem, nec meram praeteritionem sive non-electionem ad talem finem intelligere, sed simul conjungere cum decreto dandi finem, decretum praeparandi & dandi certa, designata, & infallibilia media ad finem; & cum decreto permittendi aliquem deficere a fine, aliud decretum copulare, puniendi & in aeternum damnandi ipsum qui defecit; ob hanc, inquam, causam puto melius & commodius, addo etiam verius hoc sensu, praevisum peccatum praesupponi ut conditionem subjecti, in quod cadit decretum talis praedestinationis & reprobationis. Ad Scripturam quod attinet, per praedestinationem solet denotare non nudam designationem ad finem gloriae, sed destinationem ad gloriam per media; nec per media quaelibet, sed per media gratiae efficacis derivatae a Christo Capite & Mediatore nostro. Huc faciunt illa loca; Eph. i.4. Vos elegit in ipso ut essemus sancti. 2 Tim. i.9. Servavit nos ex suo proposito & gratia, quae data est nobis in Christo ante tempora secularia. Ex quibus locis, aliisque multis quae accumulari possent, perspicuum est, Apostolum per praedestinationem intelligere destinationem & directionem ad finem gloriae per infallibilia media gratiae efficacis a Christo derivandae. De Augustino notius est quam ut multis egeat, illum per praedestinationem designare praeparationem gratiae infallibiliter perducentis ad gloriam. Celebris est illa definitio, Praedestinatio est praeparatio beneficiorum Dei, quibus certissime liberantur, quicunque liberantur. Unde Aquinas describit praedestinationem esse actum providentiae specialis ordinantis & dirigentis electos ad finem salutis, non per media quaelibet, sed per talia quae ipsum eventum infallibiliter producent. Sumatur itaque hoc: Praedestinationem prout usurpatur in Scripturis, designare non decretum abstractum, de solo fine, sed decretum quasi complicatum, de dando fine vitae aeternae per media gratiae in Christo. Jam ad Reprobationem quod attinet, ex usu Scripturarum designat non nudam praeteritionem aut non-electionem, sed praedamnationem sive deputationem ad interitum, quae inseparabili nexu cohaeret cum non-electione sive praeteritione, saltem quoad eventum. Hoc inde patet, quod reprobati vocentur in Scripturis vasa irae coagmentata ad interitum, Rom. ix.22. Olim descripti ad damnationem, Judae 4. Et Augustinus reprobationem appellat praedestinationem ad interitum. Sub reprobationis itaque vocabulo comprehendere debemus non nudum decretum praetereundi, aut non-eligendi aliquos, sed insuper voluntatem illos praedamnandi. His positis, dico talem praedestinationem & reprobationem non recte concipi aut explicari posse, nisi praeconcepto peccato, ut communi conditione in ipso subjecto.
